redshift.DescribeClusterParameterGroups.doc: Returns a list of Amazon Redshift parameter groups, including parameter groups you created and the default parameter group. For each parameter group, the response includes the parameter group name, description, and parameter group family name. You can optionally specify a name to retrieve the description of a specific parameter group. For more information about parameters and parameter groups, go to Amazon Redshift Parameter Groups in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide . If you specify both tag keys and tag values in the same request, Amazon Redshift returns all parameter groups that match any combination of the specified keys and values. For example, if you have owner and environment for tag keys, and admin and test for tag values, all parameter groups that have any combination of those values are returned. If both tag keys and values are omitted from the request, parameter groups are returned regardless of whether they have tag keys or values associated with them.

output.doc: Contains the output from the DescribeClusterParameterGroups action.

Marker.doc: A value that indicates the starting point for the next set of response records in a subsequent request. If a value is returned in a response, you can retrieve the next set of records by providing this returned marker value in the Marker parameter and retrying the command. If the Marker field is empty, all response records have been retrieved for the request.

ParameterGroups.doc: A list of ClusterParameterGroup instances. Each instance describes one cluster parameter group.

item.doc: Describes a parameter group.

ParameterGroupName.doc: The name of the cluster parameter group.

ParameterGroupFamily.doc: The name of the cluster parameter group family that this cluster parameter group is compatible with.

redshift.DescribeClusterParameters.doc: Returns a detailed list of parameters contained within the specified Amazon Redshift parameter group. For each parameter the response includes information such as parameter name, description, data type, value, whether the parameter value is modifiable, and so on. You can specify source filter to retrieve parameters of only specific type. For example, to retrieve parameters that were modified by a user action such as from ModifyClusterParameterGroup , you can specify source equal to user . For more information about parameters and parameter groups, go to Amazon Redshift Parameter Groups in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide .

output.doc: Contains the output from the DescribeClusterParameters action.

Parameters.doc: A list of Parameter instances. Each instance lists the parameters of one cluster parameter group.

item.doc: Describes a parameter in a cluster parameter group.

ParameterValue.doc: The value of the parameter. If ParameterName is wlm_json_configuration , then the maximum size of ParameterValue is 8000 characters.

Source.doc: The source of the parameter value, such as "engine-default" or "user".

DataType.doc: The data type of the parameter.

AllowedValues.doc: The valid range of values for the parameter.

ApplyType.doc: Specifies how to apply the WLM configuration parameter. Some properties can be applied dynamically, while other properties require that any associated clusters be rebooted for the configuration changes to be applied. For more information about parameters and parameter groups, go to Amazon Redshift Parameter Groups in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide .

IsModifiable.doc: If true , the parameter can be modified. Some parameters have security or operational implications that prevent them from being changed.

MinimumEngineVersion.doc: The earliest engine version to which the parameter can apply.

If the Marker field is empty, all response records have been retrieved for the request.

redshift.DescribeClusterSecurityGroups.doc: Returns information about Amazon Redshift security groups. If the name of a security group is specified, the response will contain only information about only that security group. For information about managing security groups, go to Amazon Redshift Cluster Security Groups in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide . If you specify both tag keys and tag values in the same request, Amazon Redshift returns all security groups that match any combination of the specified keys and values. For example, if you have owner and environment for tag keys, and admin and test for tag values, all security groups that have any combination of those values are returned. If both tag keys and values are omitted from the request, security groups are returned regardless of whether they have tag keys or values associated with them.

redshift.DescribeClusterSnapshots.doc: Returns one or more snapshot objects, which contain metadata about your cluster snapshots. By default, this operation returns information about all snapshots of all clusters that are owned by your Amazon Web Services account. No information is returned for snapshots owned by inactive Amazon Web Services accounts. If you specify both tag keys and tag values in the same request, Amazon Redshift returns all snapshots that match any combination of the specified keys and values. For example, if you have owner and environment for tag keys, and admin and test for tag values, all snapshots that have any combination of those values are returned. Only snapshots that you own are returned in the response; shared snapshots are not returned with the tag key and tag value request parameters. If both tag keys and values are omitted from the request, snapshots are returned regardless of whether they have tag keys or values associated with them.

output.doc: Contains the output from the DescribeClusterSnapshots action.

Marker.doc: A value that indicates the starting point for the next set of response records in a subsequent request. If a value is returned in a response, you can retrieve the next set of records by providing this returned marker value in the Marker parameter and retrying the command. If the Marker field is empty, all response records have been retrieved for the request.

item.doc: Describes a snapshot.

SnapshotIdentifier.doc: The snapshot identifier that is provided in the request.

ClusterIdentifier.doc: The identifier of the cluster for which the snapshot was taken.

SnapshotCreateTime.doc: The time (in UTC format) when Amazon Redshift began the snapshot. A snapshot contains a copy of the cluster data as of this exact time.

Status.doc: The snapshot status. The value of the status depends on the API operation used: CreateClusterSnapshot and CopyClusterSnapshot returns status as "creating". DescribeClusterSnapshots returns status as "creating", "available", "final snapshot", or "failed". DeleteClusterSnapshot returns status as "deleted".

Port.doc: The port that the cluster is listening on.

AvailabilityZone.doc: The Availability Zone in which the cluster was created.

ClusterCreateTime.doc: The time (UTC) when the cluster was originally created.

MasterUsername.doc: The admin user name for the cluster.

ClusterVersion.doc: The version ID of the Amazon Redshift engine that is running on the cluster.

EngineFullVersion.doc: The cluster version of the cluster used to create the snapshot. For example, 1.0.15503.

SnapshotType.doc: The snapshot type. Snapshots created using CreateClusterSnapshot and CopyClusterSnapshot are of type "manual".

NodeType.doc: The node type of the nodes in the cluster.

NumberOfNodes.doc: The number of nodes in the cluster.

DBName.doc: The name of the database that was created when the cluster was created.

VpcId.doc: The VPC identifier of the cluster if the snapshot is from a cluster in a VPC. Otherwise, this field is not in the output.

Encrypted.doc: If true , the data in the snapshot is encrypted at rest.

KmsKeyId.doc: The Key Management Service (KMS) key ID of the encryption key that was used to encrypt data in the cluster from which the snapshot was taken.

EncryptedWithHSM.doc: A boolean that indicates whether the snapshot data is encrypted using the HSM keys of the source cluster. true indicates that the data is encrypted using HSM keys.

AccountsWithRestoreAccess.doc: A list of the Amazon Web Services accounts authorized to restore the snapshot. Returns null if no accounts are authorized. Visible only to the snapshot owner.

item.doc: Describes an Amazon Web Services account authorized to restore a snapshot.

AccountId.doc: The identifier of an Amazon Web Services account authorized to restore a snapshot.

AccountAlias.doc: The identifier of an Amazon Web Services support account authorized to restore a snapshot. For Amazon Web Services Support, the identifier is amazon-redshift-support .

OwnerAccount.doc: For manual snapshots, the Amazon Web Services account used to create or copy the snapshot. For automatic snapshots, the owner of the cluster. The owner can perform all snapshot actions, such as sharing a manual snapshot.

TotalBackupSizeInMegaBytes.doc: The size of the complete set of backup data that would be used to restore the cluster.

ActualIncrementalBackupSizeInMegaBytes.doc: The size of the incremental backup.

BackupProgressInMegaBytes.doc: The number of megabytes that have been transferred to the snapshot backup.

CurrentBackupRateInMegaBytesPerSecond.doc: The number of megabytes per second being transferred to the snapshot backup. Returns 0 for a completed backup.

EstimatedSecondsToCompletion.doc: The estimate of the time remaining before the snapshot backup will complete. Returns 0 for a completed backup.

ElapsedTimeInSeconds.doc: The amount of time an in-progress snapshot backup has been running, or the amount of time it took a completed backup to finish.

SourceRegion.doc: The source region from which the snapshot was copied.

Tags.doc: The list of tags for the cluster snapshot.

item.doc: A tag consisting of a name/value pair for a resource.

Key.doc: The key, or name, for the resource tag.

Value.doc: The value for the resource tag.

RestorableNodeTypes.doc: The list of node types that this cluster snapshot is able to restore into.

EnhancedVpcRouting.doc: An option that specifies whether to create the cluster with enhanced VPC routing enabled. To create a cluster that uses enhanced VPC routing, the cluster must be in a VPC. For more information, see Enhanced VPC Routing in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide. If this option is true , enhanced VPC routing is enabled. Default: false

MaintenanceTrackName.doc: The name of the maintenance track for the snapshot.

ManualSnapshotRetentionPeriod.doc: The number of days that a manual snapshot is retained. If the value is -1, the manual snapshot is retained indefinitely. The value must be either -1 or an integer between 1 and 3,653.

ManualSnapshotRemainingDays.doc: The number of days until a manual snapshot will pass its retention period.

SnapshotRetentionStartTime.doc: A timestamp representing the start of the retention period for the snapshot.

MasterPasswordSecretArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the cluster's admin user credentials secret.

MasterPasswordSecretKmsKeyId.doc: The ID of the Key Management Service (KMS) key used to encrypt and store the cluster's admin credentials secret.

SnapshotArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the snapshot.

redshift.DescribeClusters.doc: Returns properties of provisioned clusters including general cluster properties, cluster database properties, maintenance and backup properties, and security and access properties. This operation supports pagination. For more information about managing clusters, go to Amazon Redshift Clusters in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide . If you specify both tag keys and tag values in the same request, Amazon Redshift returns all clusters that match any combination of the specified keys and values. For example, if you have owner and environment for tag keys, and admin and test for tag values, all clusters that have any combination of those values are returned. If both tag keys and values are omitted from the request, clusters are returned regardless of whether they have tag keys or values associated with them.

output.doc: Contains the output from the DescribeClusters action.

Marker.doc: A value that indicates the starting point for the next set of response records in a subsequent request. If a value is returned in a response, you can retrieve the next set of records by providing this returned marker value in the Marker parameter and retrying the command. If the Marker field is empty, all response records have been retrieved for the request.

Clusters.doc: A list of Cluster objects, where each object describes one cluster.

item.doc: Describes a cluster.

ClusterIdentifier.doc: The unique identifier of the cluster.

NodeType.doc: The node type for the nodes in the cluster.

ClusterStatus.doc: The current state of the cluster. Possible values are the following: available available, prep-for-resize available, resize-cleanup cancelling-resize creating deleting final-snapshot hardware-failure incompatible-hsm incompatible-network incompatible-parameters incompatible-restore modifying paused rebooting renaming resizing rotating-keys storage-full updating-hsm

ClusterAvailabilityStatus.doc: The availability status of the cluster for queries. Possible values are the following: Available - The cluster is available for queries. Unavailable - The cluster is not available for queries. Maintenance - The cluster is intermittently available for queries due to maintenance activities. Modifying - The cluster is intermittently available for queries due to changes that modify the cluster. Failed - The cluster failed and is not available for queries.

ModifyStatus.doc: The status of a modify operation, if any, initiated for the cluster.

MasterUsername.doc: The admin user name for the cluster. This name is used to connect to the database that is specified in the DBName parameter.

DBName.doc: The name of the initial database that was created when the cluster was created. This same name is returned for the life of the cluster. If an initial database was not specified, a database named dev dev was created by default.

Address.doc: The DNS address of the Cluster.

Port.doc: The port that the database engine is listening on.

item.doc: The connection endpoint for connecting to an Amazon Redshift cluster through the proxy.

VpcEndpointId.doc: The connection endpoint ID for connecting an Amazon Redshift cluster through the proxy.

VpcId.doc: The VPC identifier that the endpoint is associated.

NetworkInterfaces.doc: One or more network interfaces of the endpoint. Also known as an interface endpoint.

item.doc: Describes a network interface.

PrivateIpAddress.doc: The IPv4 address of the network interface within the subnet.

Ipv6Address.doc: The IPv6 address of the network interface within the subnet.

ClusterCreateTime.doc: The date and time that the cluster was created.

AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod.doc: The number of days that automatic cluster snapshots are retained.

ManualSnapshotRetentionPeriod.doc: The default number of days to retain a manual snapshot. If the value is -1, the snapshot is retained indefinitely. This setting doesn't change the retention period of existing snapshots. The value must be either -1 or an integer between 1 and 3,653.

ClusterSecurityGroups.doc: A list of cluster security group that are associated with the cluster. Each security group is represented by an element that contains ClusterSecurityGroup.Name and ClusterSecurityGroup.Status subelements. Cluster security groups are used when the cluster is not created in an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Clusters that are created in a VPC use VPC security groups, which are listed by the VpcSecurityGroups parameter.

ClusterSecurityGroupName.doc: The name of the cluster security group.

Status.doc: The status of the cluster security group.

VpcSecurityGroups.doc: A list of Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) security groups that are associated with the cluster. This parameter is returned only if the cluster is in a VPC.

item.doc: Describes the members of a VPC security group.

VpcSecurityGroupId.doc: The identifier of the VPC security group.

Status.doc: The status of the VPC security group.

ClusterParameterGroups.doc: The list of cluster parameter groups that are associated with this cluster. Each parameter group in the list is returned with its status.

item.doc: Describes the status of a parameter group.

ParameterGroupName.doc: The name of the cluster parameter group.

ClusterParameterStatusList.doc: The list of parameter statuses. For more information about parameters and parameter groups, go to Amazon Redshift Parameter Groups in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide .

item.doc: Describes the status of a parameter group.

ParameterApplyStatus.doc: The status of the parameter that indicates whether the parameter is in sync with the database, waiting for a cluster reboot, or encountered an error when being applied. The following are possible statuses and descriptions. in-sync : The parameter value is in sync with the database. pending-reboot : The parameter value will be applied after the cluster reboots. applying : The parameter value is being applied to the database. invalid-parameter : Cannot apply the parameter value because it has an …

ParameterApplyErrorDescription.doc: The error that prevented the parameter from being applied to the database.

ClusterSubnetGroupName.doc: The name of the subnet group that is associated with the cluster. This parameter is valid only when the cluster is in a VPC.

VpcId.doc: The identifier of the VPC the cluster is in, if the cluster is in a VPC.

AvailabilityZone.doc: The name of the Availability Zone in which the cluster is located.

PreferredMaintenanceWindow.doc: The weekly time range, in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC), during which system maintenance can occur.

PendingModifiedValues.doc: A value that, if present, indicates that changes to the cluster are pending. Specific pending changes are identified by subelements.

NodeType.doc: The pending or in-progress change of the cluster's node type.

ClusterVersion.doc: The pending or in-progress change of the service version.

AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod.doc: The pending or in-progress change of the automated snapshot retention period.

ClusterIdentifier.doc: The pending or in-progress change of the new identifier for the cluster.

PubliclyAccessible.doc: The pending or in-progress change of the ability to connect to the cluster from the public network.

EnhancedVpcRouting.doc: An option that specifies whether to create the cluster with enhanced VPC routing enabled. To create a cluster that uses enhanced VPC routing, the cluster must be in a VPC. For more information, see Enhanced VPC Routing in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide. If this option is true , enhanced VPC routing is enabled. Default: false

MaintenanceTrackName.doc: The name of the maintenance track that the cluster will change to during the next maintenance window.

EncryptionType.doc: The encryption type for a cluster. Possible values are: KMS and None.

ClusterVersion.doc: The version ID of the Amazon Redshift engine that is running on the cluster.

AllowVersionUpgrade.doc: A boolean value that, if true , indicates that major version upgrades will be applied automatically to the cluster during the maintenance window.

NumberOfNodes.doc: The number of compute nodes in the cluster.

PubliclyAccessible.doc: A boolean value that, if true , indicates that the cluster can be accessed from a public network. Default: false

Encrypted.doc: A boolean value that, if true , indicates that data in the cluster is encrypted at rest.

RestoreStatus.doc: A value that describes the status of a cluster restore action. This parameter returns null if the cluster was not created by restoring a snapshot.

Status.doc: The status of the restore action. Returns starting, restoring, completed, or failed.

CurrentRestoreRateInMegaBytesPerSecond.doc: The number of megabytes per second being transferred from the backup storage. Returns the average rate for a completed backup. This field is only updated when you restore to DC2 node types.

SnapshotSizeInMegaBytes.doc: The size of the set of snapshot data used to restore the cluster. This field is only updated when you restore to DC2 node types.

ProgressInMegaBytes.doc: The number of megabytes that have been transferred from snapshot storage. This field is only updated when you restore to DC2 node types.

ElapsedTimeInSeconds.doc: The amount of time an in-progress restore has been running, or the amount of time it took a completed restore to finish. This field is only updated when you restore to DC2 node types.

EstimatedTimeToCompletionInSeconds.doc: The estimate of the time remaining before the restore will complete. Returns 0 for a completed restore. This field is only updated when you restore to DC2 node types.

Status.doc: Describes the status of the cluster. While the transfer is in progress the status is transferringdata .

CurrentRateInMegaBytesPerSecond.doc: Describes the data transfer rate in MB's per second.

TotalDataInMegaBytes.doc: Describes the total amount of data to be transfered in megabytes.

DataTransferredInMegaBytes.doc: Describes the total amount of data that has been transfered in MB's.

EstimatedTimeToCompletionInSeconds.doc: Describes the estimated number of seconds remaining to complete the transfer.

ElapsedTimeInSeconds.doc: Describes the number of seconds that have elapsed during the data transfer.

HsmStatus.doc: A value that reports whether the Amazon Redshift cluster has finished applying any hardware security module (HSM) settings changes specified in a modify cluster command. Values: active, applying

HsmClientCertificateIdentifier.doc: Specifies the name of the HSM client certificate the Amazon Redshift cluster uses to retrieve the data encryption keys stored in an HSM.

HsmConfigurationIdentifier.doc: Specifies the name of the HSM configuration that contains the information the Amazon Redshift cluster can use to retrieve and store keys in an HSM.

Status.doc: Reports whether the Amazon Redshift cluster has finished applying any HSM settings changes specified in a modify cluster command. Values: active, applying

ClusterSnapshotCopyStatus.doc: A value that returns the destination region and retention period that are configured for cross-region snapshot copy.

DestinationRegion.doc: The destination region that snapshots are automatically copied to when cross-region snapshot copy is enabled.

RetentionPeriod.doc: The number of days that automated snapshots are retained in the destination region after they are copied from a source region.

ManualSnapshotRetentionPeriod.doc: The number of days that automated snapshots are retained in the destination region after they are copied from a source region. If the value is -1, the manual snapshot is retained indefinitely. The value must be either -1 or an integer between 1 and 3,653.

SnapshotCopyGrantName.doc: The name of the snapshot copy grant.

ClusterPublicKey.doc: The public key for the cluster.

item.doc: The identifier of a node in a cluster.

NodeRole.doc: Whether the node is a leader node or a compute node.

PrivateIPAddress.doc: The private IP address of a node within a cluster.

PublicIPAddress.doc: The public IP address of a node within a cluster.

ElasticIpStatus.doc: The status of the elastic IP (EIP) address.

ElasticIp.doc: The elastic IP (EIP) address for the cluster.

Status.doc: The status of the elastic IP (EIP) address.

ClusterRevisionNumber.doc: The specific revision number of the database in the cluster.

Tags.doc: The list of tags for the cluster.

item.doc: A tag consisting of a name/value pair for a resource.

Key.doc: The key, or name, for the resource tag.

Value.doc: The value for the resource tag.

KmsKeyId.doc: The Key Management Service (KMS) key ID of the encryption key used to encrypt data in the cluster.

EnhancedVpcRouting.doc: An option that specifies whether to create the cluster with enhanced VPC routing enabled. To create a cluster that uses enhanced VPC routing, the cluster must be in a VPC. For more information, see Enhanced VPC Routing in the Amazon Redshift Cluster Management Guide. If this option is true , enhanced VPC routing is enabled. Default: false

IamRoles.doc: A list of Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles that can be used by the cluster to access other Amazon Web Services services.

item.doc: An Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that can be used by the associated Amazon Redshift cluster to access other Amazon Web Services services.

IamRoleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role, for example, arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftCopyUnload .

ApplyStatus.doc: A value that describes the status of the IAM role's association with an Amazon Redshift cluster. The following are possible statuses and descriptions. in-sync : The role is available for use by the cluster. adding : The role is in the process of being associated with the cluster. removing : The role is in the process of being disassociated with the cluster.

PendingActions.doc: Cluster operations that are waiting to be started.

MaintenanceTrackName.doc: The name of the maintenance track for the cluster.

ElasticResizeNumberOfNodeOptions.doc: The number of nodes that you can resize the cluster to with the elastic resize method.

DeferredMaintenanceWindows.doc: Describes a group of DeferredMaintenanceWindow objects.

item.doc: Describes a deferred maintenance window

DeferMaintenanceIdentifier.doc: A unique identifier for the maintenance window.

DeferMaintenanceStartTime.doc: A timestamp for the beginning of the time period when we defer maintenance.

DeferMaintenanceEndTime.doc: A timestamp for the end of the time period when we defer maintenance.

SnapshotScheduleIdentifier.doc: A unique identifier for the cluster snapshot schedule.

SnapshotScheduleState.doc: The current state of the cluster snapshot schedule.

ExpectedNextSnapshotScheduleTime.doc: The date and time when the next snapshot is expected to be taken for clusters with a valid snapshot schedule and backups enabled.

ExpectedNextSnapshotScheduleTimeStatus.doc: The status of next expected snapshot for clusters having a valid snapshot schedule and backups enabled. Possible values are the following: OnTrack - The next snapshot is expected to be taken on time. Pending - The next snapshot is pending to be taken.

NextMaintenanceWindowStartTime.doc: The date and time in UTC when system maintenance can begin.

ResizeInfo.doc: Returns the following: AllowCancelResize: a boolean value indicating if the resize operation can be cancelled. ResizeType: Returns ClassicResize

AllowCancelResize.doc: A boolean value indicating if the resize operation can be cancelled.

AvailabilityZoneRelocationStatus.doc: Describes the status of the Availability Zone relocation operation.

ClusterNamespaceArn.doc: The namespace Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the cluster.

TotalStorageCapacityInMegaBytes.doc: The total storage capacity of the cluster in megabytes.

AquaConfiguration.doc: This field is retired. Amazon Redshift automatically determines whether to use AQUA (Advanced Query Accelerator).

AquaStatus.doc: This field is retired. Amazon Redshift automatically determines whether to use AQUA (Advanced Query Accelerator).

AquaConfigurationStatus.doc: This field is retired. Amazon Redshift automatically determines whether to use AQUA (Advanced Query Accelerator).

DefaultIamRoleArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the IAM role set as default for the cluster.

ReservedNodeExchangeStatus.doc: The status of the reserved-node exchange request. Statuses include in-progress and requested.

ReservedNodeExchangeRequestId.doc: The identifier of the reserved-node exchange request.

RequestTime.doc: A date and time that indicate when the reserved-node exchange was requested.

SourceReservedNodeId.doc: The identifier of the source reserved node.

SourceReservedNodeType.doc: The source reserved-node type, for example ra3.4xlarge.

SourceReservedNodeCount.doc: The source reserved-node count in the cluster.

TargetReservedNodeOfferingId.doc: The identifier of the target reserved node offering.

TargetReservedNodeType.doc: The node type of the target reserved node, for example ra3.4xlarge.

TargetReservedNodeCount.doc: The count of target reserved nodes in the cluster.

CustomDomainName.doc: The custom domain name associated with the cluster.

CustomDomainCertificateArn.doc: The certificate Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the custom domain name.

CustomDomainCertificateExpiryDate.doc: The expiration date for the certificate associated with the custom domain name.

MasterPasswordSecretArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the cluster's admin user credentials secret.

MasterPasswordSecretKmsKeyId.doc: The ID of the Key Management Service (KMS) key used to encrypt and store the cluster's admin credentials secret.

IpAddressType.doc: The IP address type for the cluster. Possible values are ipv4 and dualstack .

MultiAZ.doc: A boolean value that, if true, indicates that the cluster is deployed in two Availability Zones.

MultiAZSecondary.doc: The secondary compute unit of a cluster, if Multi-AZ deployment is turned on.

AvailabilityZone.doc: The name of the Availability Zone in which the secondary compute unit of the cluster is located.

ClusterNodes.doc: The nodes in the secondary compute unit.

item.doc: The identifier of a node in a cluster.

NodeRole.doc: Whether the node is a leader node or a compute node.

PrivateIPAddress.doc: The private IP address of a node within a cluster.

PublicIPAddress.doc: The public IP address of a node within a cluster.

redshift.DescribeLoggingStatus.doc: Describes whether information, such as queries and connection attempts, is being logged for the specified Amazon Redshift cluster.

output.doc: Describes the status of logging for a cluster.

LoggingEnabled.doc: true if logging is on, false if logging is off.

BucketName.doc: The name of the S3 bucket where the log files are stored.

S3KeyPrefix.doc: The prefix applied to the log file names.

LastSuccessfulDeliveryTime.doc: The last time that logs were delivered.

LastFailureTime.doc: The last time when logs failed to be delivered.

LastFailureMessage.doc: The message indicating that logs failed to be delivered.

LogDestinationType.doc: The log destination type. An enum with possible values of s3 and cloudwatch .

LogExports.doc: The collection of exported log types. Possible values are connectionlog , useractivitylog , and userlog .
